titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 147, the seven gates, part 2
part: Spell 147 — the seven gates: the fourth to the seventh gate (Plates 11–12)
work: Book of the Dead of Ani
workEn: Book of the Dead of Ani
draftNote: Draft — the hieroglyphs are read from the printed type of Budge's 1895 edition of the papyrus, and the signs and readings are still being checked; expect changes.
source: Papyrus of Ani (British Museum EA 10470), Plates XI, XII. Hieroglyphs transcribed from the interlinear text of E. A. W. Budge, The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum (London, 1895), pp. 59–63; Budge's transliteration and word-by-word English were used to check the reading of the signs and the sense, never for wording. Only the papyrus's own text is given: the passages Budge supplies from other papyri in his appendixes and footnotes are left out. Transliteration in the Leiden convention, with the reed written i; translation made fresh from the Egyptian. Shown left to right; the papyrus is written in columns read from the top down. The line under each word ("say") is the conventional Egyptological classroom pronunciation — a neutral e between consonants; ꜣ and ꜥ as a; w as u or w; ṯ as tj; ḏ as dj; ḫ and ẖ as kh; š as sh — an artificial teaching pronunciation, since the vowels of Egyptian were never written. The grouping of signs within a word follows Budge's type, which regularises the scribe's hand.
about: This part gives the second half of Spell 147, the fourth to the seventh of the gates (ꜥryt) of the realm of Osiris, along the upper register of Plates 11 and 12 of Ani's papyrus. At each gate the dead man names its doorkeeper, watcher and announcer, and then tells what he has done for Osiris: he has brought him life and the parts of his body, driven off Apep, and protected the god's eye. Budge numbers the lines afresh in each gate. Most of the gatekeepers' names and several phrases are doubtful, and the speech at the sixth gate breaks off where Budge prints a row of dots.

sentences.i: The fourth gate.
sentences.n: ꜥryt 'gate' as in the first part of the spell: the arm ꜥ, r, two reeds and t, with the house sign as classifier (Budge: ārit, 'hall'). fdnwt 'fourth' is four strokes, the numeral four (fdw), with the pot nw and t: the ordinal fdnw, which adds -nw to the numeral, feminine to agree with ꜥryt (Budge: àft). This unit opens the fourth gate; unlike the headings of the other gates, these two words are written in black. Budge starts his line numbers again at 1 in each gate, and the fourth gate runs over his lines 1 to 9. As at the first three gates, the dead man names the gate's doorkeeper, watcher and announcer, and then speaks.

Khesef-her-asha-kheru, perhaps 'Repelling of face, many of voices' (?), the doorkeeper of the fourth gate of Spell 147 (name of a gatekeeper demon; from ḫsf 'repel, drive back', ḥr 'face', ꜥšꜣ 'many' and ḫrw 'voice'; the sense of the whole is doubtful; Budge: χesef-ḥrà-āśt-χeru)

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Khesef-her-asha-kheru.
sentences.n: rn n iry-ꜥꜣ·s 'the name of its doorkeeper' as at the first gate: rn with the man with hand to mouth (A2) as classifier; the genitive n; the herdsman sign for iry, the sign coded O29 (approximate) for ꜥꜣ 'door', the low sign U15 (not read) and ·s, the gate's. The name is two of Budge's groups, joined here as one word. ḫsf is the spindle-and-viper sign ḫsf (U35) with U15, 'repel, drive back'; ḥr 'face' is the face with its stroke and a seated god; ꜥšꜣ 'many' is the lizard with plural strokes (Budge's numeral 3 is printed after it); ḫrw 'voice' is the oar with w and the man with hand to mouth. 'Repelling of face, many of voices' (?) follows the words (Budge: χesef-ḥrà-āśt-χeru), perhaps a noisy keeper who turns faces away; the sense of the whole is doubtful.

Seres-tep, perhaps 'Watchful of head' (?), the watcher of the fourth gate of Spell 147 (name of a gatekeeper demon; from srs 'make watchful', the causative of rs 'wake', and tp 'head'; the reading rests on an uncertain sign; Budge: Se-res-ṭepu)

sentences.i: The name of the watcher: Seres-tep.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes rn n in red. sꜣwty 'watcher' is the herdsman sign sꜣw with ꜣ, two reeds y, t and the low sign U15, as at the second gate, but no ·s 'its' is written here. The name is the bolt s and an upright with a hook at the top (coded T13, approximate, as for the third gate's watcher) for rs 'wake', with the eye as classifier: srs 'make watchful'; then the head tp with a stroke, a second stroke and the seated god (Budge: Se-res-ṭepu, reading the strokes as -u). 'Watchful of head' (?) on the pattern of srs-ḥr at the third gate; the reading rests on the same uncertain sign.

sentences.i: I am the bull, the son of the kite of Osiris.
sentences.n: The speech begins. ink 'I am' is the pot and the basket, here with a bold stroke in place of the seated man. kꜣ 'bull' is the raised arms kꜣ (D28) with the low sign U15 under them and the bull as classifier (Budge: ka). sꜣ 'son' is the pintail duck with its stroke, the noun before a direct genitive. ḏryt is a bundle sign (coded M36, approximate) for ḏr, with r, two reeds y and t, and a bird (coded G39, approximate, like the duck of sꜣ; a bird of prey would be expected): ḏryt 'kite', the bird of prey, the form in which Isis mourns Osiris (Budge: t'erit, 'the ancestress'). nt is the genitive in its feminine form, agreeing with ḏryt. The bull, son of Isis, is Horus, and the dead man speaks as Horus, Osiris's son and helper.

sentences.i: See, his father bears witness for him, the lord of his company(?).
sentences.n: m·tn 'see, behold' is the owl m with the arm (printed at its upper right, not read, as in mk), then t and n with plural strokes: the particle mk in the form used to more than one person, here the beings of the gate (Budge reads mā-ten, as a request). Budge's group meter-nef is split here into mtr and n·f. mtr is the hooked sign coded D53 (the house reading, approximate) for mt, with t, r, two strokes and the man with hand to mouth, the classifier of speech: mtr 'bear witness', a sḏm·f whose subject, itf·f 'his father', comes after the dative n·f 'for him' (water n and the viper, the viper restored by Budge inside his square brackets). itf·f is a reed, t and f with the seated man, and ·f. The n could instead be the n of a sḏm·n·f, 'he has borne witness'; n·f 'for him' gives the clearer sense. nb 'the lord' is the basket. imw·f is a reed, a tree-like sign (coded M1) read im, m (Budge's numeral 8 stands here, inside the word), w, the seated god with a stroke, and ·f: taken as a plural noun for the beings around a god, 'his company' (Budge: àmmu, 'divine companions'); the reading and the sense are doubtful. The father is Osiris, and 'him' is the speaker, his son.

sentences.n: wḏꜥ·n·i is w, the cobra ḏ, a thin flat sign coded D36 for ꜥ, and the sign wḏꜥ (Aa21) closing the word as its classifier, then water n and the seated man: the sḏm·n·f of wḏꜥ 'judge', 'I have judged' (Budge: ut'ā-nà; he prints his English in braces). bgꜣsw is b, a cup sign coded W11 (approximate) for g, ꜣ, the bolt s and w with plural strokes, a plural noun (Budge: beḳasu, 'the guilty'). sentences.l: (iw) · have-brought-I-him · life · to · nose-his · for · ever
sentences.i: I have brought him life, to his nose, for ever.
sentences.n: iw opens the statement and is not translated. in·n·i is the sign coded W25 (approximate; the house reading for in) with n, then the n of the sḏm·n·f and the seated man: 'I have brought', from ini 'bring'. The horned viper after it is taken, with Budge, as 'him', the one who receives life; the regular object would be the dependent pronoun sw, and the ·f may be a slip for n·f 'to him'. Either way life is brought to him. ꜥnḫ 'life' is the ankh with n and ḫ. r 'to'. fnḏ·f 'his nose' is water n printed over the viper f, then the hand d (for ḏ, as often in later writing), the nose with a stroke, and ·f (Budge: fenṭ-f). n ḏt 'for ever' is the preposition n with ḏt 'everlastingness', the cobra ḏ and t with the land sign. Life is given to the nose as breath.

The name runs from the foot of Budge's p. 60 to the top of p. 61, in two groups joined here as one word: the hand d and b, the face ḥr with its stroke, the basket k and the shelter h (Budge's numeral 6 between them), ꜣ and a small pair of walking legs, then ḫ, f and t with the seated god (Budge: Ṭeb-ḥrà-keha-χeft). ḥr is 'face' and ḫft may be 'against, opposite' or belong with ḫfty 'enemy'; db and khꜣ are not identified, and the name is not understood.

sentences.i: I have spat on the wounds(?).
sentences.n: The papyrus writes p, g, ꜣ and s; read psg 'spit, spit on', with s and g changed round and an ꜣ added. The classifier is a stream from the lips (coded D26, approximate), the sign of spitting, which leaves only this word; Budge reads peḳas, following the signs as they stand. Then water n and the seated man: psg·n·i 'I have spat'. nsp is water n, a hooked sign under it (coded T14, approximate; one reader took it for the tongue ns), the bolt s and p, with a knife (T30) and plural strokes: a word for cuts or wounds, the knife its classifier (Budge: nesp, 'the cuttings in the flesh'); the hooked sign is not read, and the word is doubtful. Spittle was a remedy: the speaker heals the god's wounds.

sentences.n: ir·i is the eye with the seated man: a sḏm·f of iri, 'I make, I perform' (Budge: 'I have made'; no n is written). sentences.i: I have protected him in his vindication.
sentences.n: nḏ is the sign coded Aa27 (approximate; the house reading for nḏ), the pot nw standing for its n, and the low sign U15: nḏ 'protect', the word used of Horus who protects (and avenges) his father. Budge's groups net' and en are joined here into one word, the sḏm·n·f nḏ·n 'I have protected'; its suffix ·i is not written, as often on this papyrus, and is read from the 'I' of the speech. sw 'him' is the sedge sw with w, the dependent pronoun. m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'in vindication': m (Aa15) with the noun mꜣꜥ-ḫrw, the plinth and the oar. Budge takes the words as 'he has triumphed', with en as the n of a sḏm·n·f and sw as its subject; that reading is possible, but sw does not usually stand as the subject of a verb.

sentences.i: uniting his bones, gathering his limbs.
sentences.n: dmḏ 'uniting' is the same unidentified sign as in line 7 (coded V6, approximate), read with Budge (ṭemt); the reading rests on him. qsw·f 'his bones' is the harpoon-head qs written three times for the plural, with ·f (Budge: qesu-f). sꜣq 'gather, collect' is the folded cloth s, a box-like sign coded Aa18 (approximate) for sꜣ, ꜣ, the wedge q, a low animal-like sign (coded I3, approximate; not a usual classifier of this word) and the roll (Budge: saqa). ꜥwt·f 'his limbs' is the arm ꜥ and t with a piece of flesh (F51, approximate) and a stroke, and ·f; the plural ending is not written. The two infinitives tell how the speaker has protected Osiris, by putting his body together again. The fifth gate ends here.

sentences.i: I have made the way of my going, which Anubis created(?).
sentences.n: ir·n·i wꜣt 'I have made the way', as at the fifth gate. šmt·i is a pool on walking legs printed as one sign (the sign šm, N40; coded here as the pool N37 and the legs), with m, t, walking legs again and the seated man: the infinitive šmt 'going' with ·i, 'my going', joined to wꜣt as a direct genitive (Budge: śemt-à, 'I have passed along'). Budge's groups qemam and en are joined here into one word: the wedge q and ꜣ, a throw-stick (coded T14, approximate), the sign of qmꜣ 'create', with m (Aa15) and a clump of plants (coded M15, approximate) as classifier, then water n: the relative form qmꜣ·n 'which (Anubis) created'. The plant classifier belongs rather to qmꜣ 'reed, rush', a word of the same sound. inpw 'Anubis' is a reed, n and p with the seated jackal-headed god. The relative form would take a t to agree with wꜣt, which is not written; the construction is doubtful, and 'my going' may also be a clause of its own, 'I go …'.

sentences.i: I am the lord of the Great Crown, who devises(?) magic, the protector of maat.
sentences.n: ink 'I am'. nb 'the lord', the basket. wrrt 'the Great Crown' is the swallow wr with r twice and a crown (coded S3, approximate; Budge's numeral 8 before it) as classifier; the t is not written. ḫmt is ḫ, the hooked sign mt (D53, the house reading), t, three lines (Z3A) and the arms held out (D35, approximate), as in the third gate: ḫmt 'think out, plan', taken as a participle, 'who devises'. Budge reads 'without' (χemet), as though from ḫm 'not know', whose classifier the arms are; the word is doubtful. ḥkꜣw 'magic, spells' is the wick ḥ, the raised arms kꜣ, the coil w, ꜣ and the man with hand to mouth with a stroke (Budge: ḥekau). nḏ is the sign coded Aa27 with the pot for its n and U15, here a participle used as a noun, 'the protector' (Budge: net'); mꜣꜥt 'maat, right order' is the sickle mꜣ, the arm ꜥ and t, with the plinth (Aa11), the roll and a stroke as classifiers.

sentences.i: The way has been made for the going of the Osiris Ani with you in […]
sentences.n: iry is the eye with two reeds and a stroke: taken as the passive sḏm of iri, with its y written, 'has been made' (Budge: àriu, '[I have] made'). wꜣt 'the way'. šmt is the pool-and-legs sign with m, t and walking legs, as in line 7: the infinitive 'going', which follows wꜣt as a direct genitive, as wꜣt šmt·i 'the way of my going' does there, and takes the Osiris Ani as its subject, again a direct genitive: 'the way of the going of the Osiris Ani' (Budge: śemt, 'hath passed', a finite verb). 'For' in the English renders the genitive. ḥnꜥ·tn 'with you' is the twisted wick ḥ, n and ꜥ, with t, n and plural strokes, the suffix ·tn (plural): the beings of the gate. m 'in' (Aa15). After m Budge prints a row of dots: the words that follow are lost or were not given, and the sentence breaks off. The sixth gate ends here.

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Sekhem-em-denu-sen.
sentences.n: iry-ꜥꜣ·s as before. The name is two of Budge's groups, joined here as one word. The sceptre sḫm with m gives sḫm 'be mighty, have power'. Then come the low sign U15 and t, which are not read here (Budge's second group begins with them; his Maṭenu takes its m from the owl that follows); the owl m, 'in'; the hand d, under which Budge prints '(sic)', water n and w (Budge's numeral 3 before w), with a knife (T30) and strokes, perhaps dnw 'cutting off', from dn 'sever'; and s and n with strokes, the suffix ·sn 'them', the object of the infinitive. 'Mighty in cutting them down' (?) (Budge: Seχem-Maṭenu-sen). The unread signs and Budge's sic leave the name doubtful.

sentences.i: You have made all the ways good for me before you.
sentences.n: ir·n·k is the eye, water n and ·k: the sḏm·n·f of iri, 'you have made'. Budge reads a request ('make'), which would want the imperative or a sḏm·f; as written it is a statement. n·i 'for me' is water n and the seated man. wꜣwt 'ways' is the road sign with t and plural strokes; nbt 'all' is the basket with t, and nfrt 'good' the lute nfr (F35) with f, r and t, both feminine to agree with wꜣwt. nfrt may describe the ways ('all good ways') or say what they are made ('made good'). ḫr·k 'before you', as in line 6. Spell 147 ends here; Spell 146 follows on the papyrus, in the next part.

glossary.m: m — in, from (preposition) · also "with" (instrument), "as" (m bnw "as the Bennu"), "on" (living on), "by"; im before a suffix (im·i, im·f, im·tn) · a second word of the same spelling: what? (interrogative pronoun; r m 'for what? why?') · also 'among' (with a group of people) · also the negative imperative 'do not!' (before a verb form: m irt 'do not make'; from the verb imi) · also written mꜥ, with the arm · also "of, made of" (naming the material a thing is made of)
glossary.ḫsf-ꜣd: ḫsf-ꜣd — Khesef-ad, perhaps 'Who repels the raging one' (?), the announcer of the fourth gate of Spell 147 (name of a gatekeeper demon; from ḫsf 'repel' and ꜣd 'be aggressive, rage'; Budge: χesef-Aṭ)
glossary.ḏd: ḏd — to say, speak (verb; ḏd in N "said by N", the formula that brings in a speech); ḏdt "words, speech" (noun from it)
glossary.in: in — by (naming the agent, as in ḏd in N "said by N"); (particle) it is … · a second word of the same spelling: to say, said (verb; normally after the words quoted: in·sn 'they say', in N 'says N'; in·k 'you said')
glossary.wsir: wsir — Osiris, god of the dead and king of the world below; Wsir N "the Osiris N", the dead person (god's name; Budge: Àusàr)
glossary.sš: sš — scribe (noun; the palette-and-pen sign) · a second word of the same spelling: to pass, go through (verb; doubtful here) · also to write, draw, paint (verb; written with the scribe's palette) · also the noun 'writing, document, record' (noun m.) · also to open (a door), spread open (verb; said of doors and bolts) · a further word of the same spelling: nest (noun m.; written with the nest of young birds; dual sšwy)
glossary.ꜣny: ꜣny — Ani, royal scribe of Thebes, for whom the papyrus was made (personal name)
glossary.mꜣꜥ-ḫrw: mꜣꜥ-ḫrw — true of voice, vindicated (epithet; said of the dead whose words were found true at the judgement) · also, as a noun, vindication, the being found true (m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'in vindication'; written in full or short)
glossary.ink: ink — I (1st person singular independent pronoun; ink N "I am N")
glossary.kꜣ: kꜣ — ka, the life-force that receives offerings (noun); plural kꜣw, perhaps also "food, sustenance" · a second word of the same spelling: bull (noun; written with the bull)
glossary.sꜣ: sꜣ — protection (noun; m sꜣ "for the protection of") · a second word of the same spelling: son (noun m.; the pintail-duck sign; sꜣ·k 'your son', sꜣ tpy 'eldest son') · a third word of the same spelling: back (noun; the sign Aa18; as in m-sꜣ 'behind'; Budge: sa)
glossary.ḏrt: ḏrt — kite, the bird of prey; ḏrty 'the two kites', Isis and Nephthys as mourners of Osiris (noun f.; Budge: t'ertutu)
glossary.mk: mk — behold, see (particle) · also written m·tn, mtn 'behold', when more than one person is addressed (particle with the suffix ·tn)
glossary.·tn: ·tn — you, your (2nd person plural suffix pronoun)
glossary.mtr: mtr — to bear witness, testify (verb); witness (noun; plural mtrw)
glossary.n: n — not; negates the verb ('I have not …') · also in n wn "there is not" · a second word of the same spelling: the preposition "to, for" (n·i "to me") · the negative also before a noun, 'without, there being no …' · the preposition also 'because of, on account of'
glossary.·f: ·f — he, him, his, it (3rd person masculine singular suffix pronoun; the horned viper)
glossary.itf: itf — father (noun m.; plural itw 'fathers, forefathers')
glossary.nb: nb — lord, master, possessor (of); (adjective, after a noun) every, all
glossary.imw: imw — flame, burning (?) (noun; written with the flame as classifier; not known otherwise; Budge: àmmu) · company, the following of a god (?) (noun pl.; doubtful; Budge: àmmu, 'divine companions')
glossary.wḏꜥ: wḏꜥ — to judge, separate (verb); wḏꜥ(w)t 'judgement, decision' (noun)
glossary.sḏm·n·f: sḏm·n·f — the n of the sḏm·n·f, marking a completed action ("I have …", "I …ed") (verb form; written between the verb and its suffix)
glossary.·i: ·i — I, me (1st-person singular suffix pronoun; the seated-man sign)
glossary.bgꜣsw: bgꜣsw — the guilty (?) (noun pl.; perhaps from bgꜣ 'fault, failing'; meaning doubtful; Budge: beḳasu, 'the guilty')
glossary.im: im — there, therein (adverb; nty im "he who is there")
glossary.iw: iw — opens a statement, often with a suffix (iw·f "he …"); not translated (particle)
glossary.ini: ini — to bring, fetch (verb 3ae-inf.; sḏm·n·f in·n·i 'I have brought')
glossary.ꜥnḫ: ꜥnḫ — to live; life (verb) · also living (participle or adjective after its noun; bꜣ ꜥnḫ 'a living ba')
glossary.r: r — to, towards, into, at (preposition); with an infinitive "in order to"; with the sḏmt·f "until"; after an imperative, with a suffix (ir·k), "yourself, then" · a second word of the same spelling: goose, fowl (noun; the goose sign) · also against (of hostility: r·i 'against me'); concerning, about (r·f 'concerning him')
glossary.ḏt: ḏt — everlastingness, time as unchanging permanence (noun f.; paired with nḥḥ) · a second word of the same spelling: body, person (noun f.)
glossary.ir: ir — to do, make (lemma iri) · a second word of the same spelling: the particle ir "when, if" at the head of a clause (ir ꜥq·i "when I entered"), here apparently also bringing in a question ("do you know …?") · also "as for" (particle; ir with a noun puts that noun first as the topic)
glossary.swꜣ: swꜣ — to pass, pass by (verb; swꜣ ḥr 'pass by'; written with the crossed sticks and walking legs)
glossary.ẖrt-nṯr: ẖrt-nṯr — necropolis, realm of the dead; lit. 'what is under the god' (noun f.; Budge: Neter-χert)
glossary.diwnw: diwnw — fifth (ordinal numeral, from diw 'five'; feminine diwnwt; Budge: ṭuat)
glossary.ꜥnḫ-f-m-fnṯw: ꜥnḫ-f-m-fnṯw — Ankh-ef-em-fenetju, 'He lives on worms', the doorkeeper of the fifth gate of Spell 147 (name of a gatekeeper demon; from ꜥnḫ 'live', ·f 'he', m 'on' and fnṯw 'worms'; Budge: ānχ-f-em-fent)
glossary.šꜣbw: šꜣbw — Shabu, the watcher of the fifth gate of Spell 147; the name is not understood (name of a gatekeeper demon; Budge: Śabu)
glossary.db-ḥr-khꜣ-ḫft: db-ḥr-khꜣ-ḫft — Deb-her-keha-kheft, the announcer of the fifth gate of Spell 147; the name is not understood (name of a gatekeeper demon; contains ḥr 'face' and perhaps ḫft 'against, opposite'; db and khꜣ are not identified; Budge: Ṭeb-ḥrà-keha-χeft)
glossary.ꜥrt: ꜥrt — jaw (noun f.; dual ꜥrty 'the two jaws'; Budge: ārti, 'jaw bones')
glossary.imy: imy — who/which is in (the nisba of m "in"; plural imyw)
glossary.rꜣ-sṯꜣw: rꜣ-sṯꜣw — Rosetau, the Sokar necropolis realm near Giza
glossary.·k: ·k — you, your (2nd person masculine singular suffix pronoun; the basket sign)
glossary.psd: psd — to move (?) (verb; written with a leg as classifier; the word is not known otherwise; Budge: peṭes, pest) · back, backbone (noun m.; Budge: pesṭ, 'backbone')
glossary.iwnw: iwnw — Heliopolis, the sun-cult city (Budge: Annu)
glossary.dmḏ: dmḏ — to unite, join together (verb; Budge: ṭemt)
glossary.ꜥšꜣ: ꜥšꜣ — many, numerous, much (adjective; the lizard sign) · multitude, the many (noun; with a suffix, 'its many (parts)'; Budge: āśt)
glossary.ꜥꜣpp: ꜥꜣpp — Apep, the great serpent, enemy of the sun-god (god's name; Budge: Āpep)
glossary.psg: psg — to spit, spit on (verb; Budge: pesaḳ, 'wash')
glossary.nsp: nsp — cut, wound (?) (noun; written with the knife as classifier; word doubtful; Budge: nesp, 'the cuttings in the flesh')
glossary.iꜣw: iꜣw — praise, adoration (noun) · old man, the aged one (noun; written with the bent man leaning on a stick; Budge: àau, 'the Aged one')
glossary.imytw: imytw — between, among (preposition; from the nisba imy 'which is in'; Budge: àmt)
glossary.nḏ: nḏ — to protect, guard (verb) · in the compound nḏ-ḥr 'to protect, take care of' (verb; with ḥr 'face')
glossary.sw: sw — he, him, it (3rd person masculine singular dependent pronoun)
glossary.qs: qs — bone (noun m.; plural qsw; Budge: qesu)
glossary.sꜣq: sꜣq — robbery, theft (Budge reads the damaged sin here with a query) · to gather, collect, put together (verb; Budge: saqa)
glossary.sisnw: sisnw — sixth (ordinal numeral, from sis 'six'; feminine sisnwt; Budge: saset)
glossary.itk-tꜣw-khꜣq-ḫrw: itk-tꜣw-khꜣq-ḫrw — Itek-tau-kehaq-kheru, the doorkeeper of the sixth gate of Spell 147; the name is not understood (name of a gatekeeper demon; only ḫrw 'voice' is clear, tꜣw perhaps 'loaves' (?); Budge: Àtek-tau-kehaq-χeru)
glossary.in-ḥr: in-ḥr — In-her, perhaps 'Who brings the face' (?), the watcher of the sixth gate of Spell 147 (name of a gatekeeper demon; from ini 'bring, fetch' and ḥr 'face'; doubtful; Budge: Àn-ḥrà)
glossary.ꜣds-ḥr: ꜣds-ḥr — Ades-her, perhaps 'Sharp of face' (?), the announcer of the sixth gate of Spell 147 (name of a gatekeeper demon; ꜣds not identified, its knife classifier points to cutting, ḥr 'face'; a guess; Budge: Aṭes-ḥrà)
glossary.ii: ii — to come (verb; ii·n·i "I have come")
glossary.min: min — today (adverb; written with the sun as classifier; Budge: mān, 'daily')
glossary.sp: sp — time, occasion; deed, case, matter (noun); sp sn 'twice'
glossary.sn: sn — two (numeral; sp sn 'twice', written after a word to be said twice) · a second word of the same spelling: brother; companion, fellow (noun m.) · a third word of the same spelling: them, they (3rd person plural dependent pronoun; object of a verb, or subject after a particle)
glossary.qmꜣ: qmꜣ — to create, produce, bring forth (verb)
glossary.inpw: inpw — Anubis, the jackal god of the cemetery and of embalming (god's name; Budge: Ànpu)
glossary.wrrt: wrrt — the Great Crown, a crown of the king (noun f.; from wr 'great'; Budge: ureret)
glossary.ḫmt: ḫmt — to think, intend, plan (verb); thought, intention (noun) (Budge: χemet, 'desire')
glossary.mꜣꜥt: mꜣꜥt — truth, right order (maꜥat) · also Maat, the goddess of truth and right order (god's name; the seated goddess with the feather)
glossary.irt: irt — eye (noun f.; dual irty 'the two eyes')
glossary.sšd: sšd — a word not identified here (meaning uncertain; Budge: seśeṭ, sic) · to bind up, bandage (?) (verb; a guess; Budge: seśeṭ, 'bandaged')
glossary.sfḫnw: sfḫnw — seventh (ordinal numeral, from sfḫ 'seven'; feminine sfḫnwt; Budge: seχef)
glossary.sḫm-m-dnw-sn: sḫm-m-dnw-sn — Sekhem-em-denu-sen, perhaps 'Mighty in cutting them down' (?), the doorkeeper of the seventh gate of Spell 147 (name of a gatekeeper demon; from sḫm 'be mighty', m 'in', dnw 'cutting off' (from dn 'sever') and ·sn 'them'; doubtful; Budge: Seχem-Maṭenu-sen)
glossary.ꜥꜣ-mꜣꜥ-ḫrw: ꜥꜣ-mꜣꜥ-ḫrw — Aa-maa-kheru, perhaps 'Great one, true of voice' (?), the watcher of the seventh gate of Spell 147 (name of a gatekeeper demon; from ꜥꜣ 'great' and mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice'; Budge: Āā-maāχeru)
glossary.ḫsf-ḫmiw: ḫsf-ḫmiw — Khesef-khemiu, 'Who repels the destroyers', the announcer of the seventh gate of Spell 147 (name of a gatekeeper demon; from ḫsf 'repel' and ḫmiw 'destroyers', from ḫmi 'destroy'; Budge: χesef-χemi)
glossary.ḫr: ḫr — to fall (verb) · a second word of the same spelling: to, near, with (preposition; of persons) · also 'before' (ḫr nṯrw 'before the gods')
glossary.wꜥb: wꜥb — to be pure, clean; to purify oneself, bathe (verb); pure (adjective) · also wꜥb 'wab-priest', the 'pure one', a priest of the ordinary rank (noun) · also wꜥb 'purification, purity' (noun) · also wꜥbt 'the pure place', the place of embalming (noun f.)
glossary.rḏw: rḏw — efflux, exudation, the fluids that run from a corpse (noun; Budge: ertu, 'foul emanations')
glossary.rr: rr — to go round, encircle (?) (verb; the word is not known otherwise; Budge: rer)
glossary.rꜥ: rꜥ — Ra, the sun-god (god's name; Budge: Rā) · also the sun; day (noun; rꜥ nb 'every day')
glossary.rḫyt: rḫyt — common folk, subjects (noun; written with the lapwing)
glossary.wꜥ: wꜥ — one; (as a noun) one (of), someone
glossary.ist: ist — now, see (particle opening a new statement)
glossary.sktt: sktt — Sektet, the evening bark of the sun (boat name; Budge: sektet)
glossary.ꜣḫt: ꜣḫt — horizon (noun f.; the place where the sun rises and sets; written with the sun between two hills) · a second word of the same spelling: the season of inundation (noun f.)
glossary.mri: mri — to love, wish, desire (verb; relative form mrrt·f, mrt·f 'what he loves, what he desires')
glossary.sꜥḥ: sꜥḥ — noble, dignitary (noun; plural sꜥḥw) · noble body, mummy, the noble form of the dead god (noun; Budge: sāḥ, 'mummy')
glossary.wsr: wsr — power, strength (noun); to be strong, powerful (verb); strong (adjective)
glossary.ḫpr: ḫpr — to come into being, happen, become (verb)
glossary.mi: mi — come! (the imperative that serves the verbs of coming, iwi and ii; in later copies written with the owl m and the forearm ꜥ, as if mꜥ, with the walking legs) · a second word of the same spelling: like, as (preposition)
glossary.ḥr: ḥr — face; (preposition) upon, on, over, concerning · a second word of the same spelling: Horus, the falcon god, son of Osiris and Isis; the sun as a falcon (god's name; Budge: Ḥeru) · also 'at' (ḥr sbꜣw 'at the gates'); ḥr-tp 'upon' (compound preposition: ḥr + tp 'head') · also for, on behalf of; on account of (preposition; ḥr·k 'for you')
glossary.nfr: nfr — beautiful, good, perfect (adjective; follows its noun; verb 'be good'); also beauty, goodness (noun m.)
